_note: Step-by-step clues for Calendar (Chapter 9): the book questions and the past-paper questions filed under the chapter, by question id. Each list says what to count (the days in between, or the odd days left over after whole weeks), shows the count month by month or year by year, then asks the student to move on that many days from the day they know. The last clue never gives the day. Questions marked needs-review have none. tools/check_clues.ts checks them.

ca-b01: Count the odd days (days left over after whole weeks) from the start of the calendar. 2000 whole years have 0 odd days.
In 2001: January 31 days = 3 odd days, February 28 = 0, March 3, April 2, May 3, and 1 June adds 1. That is 12.
12 = 7 + 5. With 0 = Sunday, 1 = Monday…, which day is 5?
ca-b02: One week has 7 days. Turn the 6 weeks into days first.
ca-b03: Count the odd days (days left over after whole weeks) from the start of the calendar. 1600 whole years have 0 odd days.
1 January 1601 adds 1 odd day. With 0 = Sunday, 1 = Monday, so 1 January 1601 was a Monday.
Monday is the 1st. Count on to the first Saturday: which date is it?
ca-b04: Every 7 days the weekday comes back round. So only the days left over after whole weeks matter.
From the 6th to the 14th is 14 − 6 = 8 days = 1 week + 1 day.
Count 1 days on from Friday. Which day do you reach?
ca-b05: Every 7 days the weekday comes back round. So only the days left over after whole weeks matter.
78 = 11 × 7 + 1: 11 whole weeks and 1 day left over.
Count 1 days on from Sunday. Which day do you reach?
ca-b06: One year on, the weekday moves on by 1 day (365 = 52 weeks + 1), or by 2 if a 29 February comes in between.
From 14 March 2022 to 14 March 2023 there is no 29 February (February 2023 has 28 days). So it is 365 days.
Count 1 days on from Monday. Which day do you reach?
ca-b07: 1 December is a Sunday. Count on to the first Wednesday: Monday 2, Tuesday 3, Wednesday 4.
Each Wednesday after that is 7 days later: 4, 11, …
Keep adding 7. Which date is the fourth Wednesday?
ca-b08: Two years have the same calendar when they start on the same day and are both ordinary (or both leap) years.
Each ordinary year adds 1 odd day and each leap year 2. From 1991: 1991 +1, 1992 +2, 1993 +1, … Add until you reach a multiple of 7.
1991 to 2001 add up to 14 odd days, 2 whole weeks. Which year starts next, and is it a leap year?
ca-b09: Work out today first. The day before yesterday was Saturday.
So yesterday was Sunday and today is Monday.
The day after tomorrow is 2 days after today. Which day is that?
ca-b10: Write down the dates of all the Saturdays and Sundays. Day 1 is a Saturday.
Saturdays: 1, 8, 15, 22, 29. Sundays: 2, 9, 16, 23, 30. The 2nd and 4th Saturdays are 8 and 22.
Holidays: 5 Sundays + 2 Saturdays. How many of the 30 days are left for work?
ca-b11: Count the odd days in whole centuries: 100 years = 76 ordinary + 24 leap years = 124 odd days = 5 left over after weeks.
100 years: 5 odd days (Friday). 200: 10 → 3 (Wednesday). 300: 15 → 1 (Monday). 400: 20 + 1 → 0 (Sunday). Then it repeats.
So a century can only end on a Monday, Wednesday, Friday or Sunday. Which option is one of these?
ca-b12: Every 4th year is a leap year: 100 ÷ 4 = 25.
But the 100th year is a century year, and a century year is a leap year only if it divides by 400.
In an ordinary century, take that one away from 25. How many are left?
ca-b13: Count month by month, and count both the first and last days. 1996 divides by 4, so it is a leap year.
26–31 January: 6 days. February: 29. March: 31. April: 30. 1–15 May: 15.
ca-b14: Virat only goes to the market on Sundays, so 10 days ago was a Sunday.
10 = 7 + 3: one whole week and 3 days left over.
Count 3 days on from Sunday. Which day do you reach?
ca-b15: Count the days from 26 January to 5 March 2000. 2000 divides by 400, so it is a leap year.
5 more days in January + 29 in February + 5 in March = 39 = 5 × 7 + 4.
Count 4 days on from Wednesday. Which day do you reach?
